newsitem.title: INDIA: Calcutta shares slump on hectic selling by funds.
newsitem.headline: Calcutta shares slump on hectic selling by funds.

text.p: Calcutta shares ended lower on Thursday on hectic selling by foreign institutional investors (FIIs) and local traders, brokers said.
FIIs and local traders were disappointed by the Indian finance minister's failure to offer fresh sops for capital markets while winding up the debate on the federal budget, they said.
The Calcutta index fell 0.23 points down to 439.43.

"Almost everybody has taken a dim view of the bugdet proposals. The finance minister has not shown any consideration for the capital markets. A recovery is not in sight and the immediate outlook for stock prices look bad," said Aprajit Sharma of brokers Jet Age Securities.

"Today prices recovered marginally towards close on short- covering by speculators who possibly felt that prices may have fallen too much in too short a time. But this is not likely to sustain as higher levels will attract fresh selling. Foreign funds who are the only ones with money are selling off all their favourite scrips," Sharma said.
